Ergonomics wise, I find it best to not be held (gripped), but to have it resting in open hands in a light, underhand grip, not an overhand grip (X360 pad lands in an overhand), if that makes any sense. An open hand way of holding it also improves face buttons access...

Face buttons, these are secondary to me and their functionality is replaced and enhanced by other SC features:

Back buttons replace A and B - jump action bound to back left button feels great.

Weapon zoom action, that is sometimes on a face button is amazing when put on triggers soft pull, and it can be set to have a hip shot set on quick pull, but a slower pull will bring iron-sights/zoom before shot. Add a gyro aim to this and it is a game changer.

And this brings us to SC's adaptability, you can do whatever you want with this - literally change how the game plays. This is also SC's biggest problem, because without going through the hassle of understanding hardware and software features, a new user is trying to hold, and use it like the pad they had before, and SC falls short.
